sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Establishment**: Built in **1575** at **Fatehpur Sikri** to host religious debates.
• **Evolution**: Initially restricted to Sunni Ulema, later opened to Shias, Hindus, Jains, Christians (Jesuits), and Zoroastrians by **1578**.
• **Objective**: To resolve theological disputes and find common ground between conflicting interpretations of Sharia.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The failure of the Ulema to reach a consensus led Akbar to issue the **Mahzar (1579)**, declaring himself the final arbiter in religious disputes.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Exclusive to Sunni Ulema; focus on internal Islamic jurisprudence.
Internal friction among Ulema (Makhdum-ul-Mulk vs. Sheikh Abdun Nabi).
Prelims: Understanding the shift from orthodoxy.
Inclusion of non-Muslims (Jesuits, Jains, Parsis); debates on comparative religion.
Akbar's disillusionment with narrow-mindedness of the clergy.

items.definition: A document signed by leading Ulema recognizing Akbar as the 'Imam-i-Adil' (Just Ruler), giving him the right to choose between conflicting religious interpretations.
The policy of 'universal peace' or 'absolute peace' adopted by Akbar, emphasizing tolerance and equality among all religions.
Three missions sent from Goa to Akbar's court (led by Aquaviva and Monserrate) to convert the Emperor, which failed but provided detailed historical accounts.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Intellectual Pluralism**: Breaking the monopoly of the Ulema over state policy.
• **Comparative Theology**: Systematic study of diverse scriptures leading to the synthesis of Akbar's personal religious philosophy.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Intense opposition from orthodox Sunni clergy; accusations of apostasy against Akbar.
• **Solutions**: Consolidation of power through the Mahzar and the eventual closure of the Ibadat Khana when debates became too acrimonious.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'I-M-S' (Ibadat, Mahzar, Sulh-i-kul).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Ibadat Khana (1575) -> Mahzar (1579) -> Sulh-i-kul (Policy outcome).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the Ibadat Khana with the Din-i-Ilahi. The Ibadat Khana was a debating hall; Din-i-Ilahi was a personal spiritual order/code of conduct. They are distinct.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Eclecticism' to describe Akbar's religious approach. Quote: 'Akbar's religious policy was a pragmatic tool for political stability in a multi-ethnic empire.'

keyTakeaways: The Ibadat Khana was the laboratory for Akbar's religious synthesis.
It effectively ended the political dominance of the orthodox Ulema in the Mughal state.
The transition from Ibadat Khana to Mahzar represents the shift from religious debate to imperial authority.
